body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Saturday, October 31 — Halloween — and the day's top story is a homicide investigation in southwest Bakersfield, where deputies were called to South Half Moon Drive before dawn. Otherwise, expect a mild, clear fall day: a high near 70, a current 62 degrees at Meadows Field, no active weather alerts, and air quality sitting at a healthy 36. A quiet morning for the rest of us; a hard one for one family.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's most serious call came at 3:37 a.m., when a caller reported five shots and screaming on South Half Moon Drive in southwest Bakersfield. Deputies arrived and found a victim, and callers reported subjects fleeing the area — some by vehicle, and one on foot who was seen crossing toward an apartment complex across the street. A caller also reported blood in an alleyway, and a briefing was staged near Savory Lane and South Half Moon. By 4:53 a.m., dispatch was working the call as a homicide. That investigation is active, and we'll have more as it develops.

In east Bakersfield, officers were sent to the 3500 block of Country Club Drive at 5:43 a.m., where a man was reported to have stabbed his brother in the face with a nail and to still be trying to stab people. He reportedly had several nails with him.

Earlier, shots fired on Mohawk Street at 11:49 p.m. ended with two people detained; officers said no one else was outstanding, though a search of a nearby field and a house south of it continued. Deputies also spent about an hour, from 12:05 to 1:07 a.m., searching a backyard, shed, and overhang on Hageman Road at Ledgeview Lane for a man wanted on a served criminal protective order and reported to be hiding there. An air unit watched the yard until the search was cleared.

Four separate calls about people with firearms came in across the evening and early morning — at the Camilla Village apartments, at Valley Plaza and Castro Lane, at an apartment complex on Terrace Way, and on Quincy Street, where a neighbor was reported to have pointed a laser at the caller. A vehicle struck a pedestrian at 30th Street and Union Avenue just before midnight, and two traffic stops turned into foot chases — one at Fremont Street and 9th Avenue, another at South Fairfax Road and Oasis.

## Today's weather

A pleasant fall Saturday is on tap. The high should reach near 70 degrees, with a low around 57 tonight — comfortable for trick-or-treaters once the sun goes down, though you'll want a jacket after dark. It's currently 62 degrees at Meadows Field. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, no active fires reported, and air quality is good at an index of 36. In short: about as nice a Halloween as the valley gives us.

## Top stories

**Bakersfield police are searching for a suspect in a burglary at the Smoke Bros shop on Rosedale Highway, according to Bakersfield Now.** Few details were available by this morning, but the department has asked the public to help identify whoever is responsible. We'll pass along any description or tip line information as soon as it's released.

**KGET 17 reports that GET will offer free rides to veterans and active-duty military members throughout November.** The promotion gives local service members a no-cost way to get around Bakersfield and Kern County for the full month, a small thank-you timed to Veterans Day. It's a straightforward benefit worth passing along to anyone who served.

**According to 23ABC, downtown Bakersfield businesses are frustrated that construction has torn up sidewalks right before Halloween, one of their busiest nights of the year.** Parts of Wall Street are unpaved, and customers have had to navigate dirt and steps to reach front doors — one person in a wheelchair had to roll in through the dirt. Trisha Fike, owner of Guthrie's, told the station the timing of the California Water Service project stings, saying if crews had waited until January, businesses could have gotten through the holidays smoothly. Marc Deleon of Mad Dog Tattoos said a project that should have wrapped in early October is still going near 18th and 19th streets. For small downtown shops that count on holiday revenue, the calendar matters as much as the concrete.

**23ABC also shared the story of a community baby shower that has turned local donations into year-round support for families.** Kristy Elias was 18 and finishing high school when she learned she was pregnant; she credits the Bakersfield Pregnancy Center with giving her the confidence to become a mother, and 13 years later her son Jaden is a teenager. Jordan Watson and his wife, expecting their first child in December, have leaned on the center's classes too. Executive Director Erin Rogers said the center offers its services free and relies on community donations — diapers, wipes, formula, clothing — to keep them going.

**Kern County and CSUB have launched a partnership bringing $500,000 to create 50 paid internships at local workplaces, 23ABC reported.** CSUB president Vernon Harper said the county is allocating the money through its employer training resource, and Cornerstone Engineering partner Eric Dhanens said his firm has hired 10 to 20 people in the past six to twelve months. Student Rachelle Barreyro, who hopes to become a research scientist, called the local focus special. For students trying to get from a classroom to a career, paid experience close to home is often the difference.

**KGET 17 has Week 11 high school football coverage from around Bakersfield and Kern County**, and a Halloween-appropriate piece on a ghost tour of three downtown staples. Both are worth a look if you're planning your Saturday.

## Something good

If you know a veteran or someone on active duty, tell them about GET's November promotion — free rides all month, no fine print to decode. And if you've got a spare pack of diapers or a can of formula, the Bakersfield Pregnancy Center turns those donations into real help for parents who are nervous and doing their best. Kindness that practical is worth celebrating.

## Coming up this week

A few meetings and events are on the calendar. The Police Civil Service Commission meets Wednesday, November 4 at 8:30 a.m. City Council holds two sessions that same day — one at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m. — so check the agenda for which items land where. The Planning Commission meets Thursday, November 5 at 5:30 p.m.

Over at the Fox Theater, the calendar is filling up: Journey USA plays November 7, along with Texas Tornado Tradition the same day, followed by Cults & Classics: Play Misty for Me on November 9, the Nutcracker! Magical Christmas Ballet on November 13, and the 20th Anniversary of the Bakersfield Country Music Awards on November 15. And a season pass is already on sale for Cults & Classics 2026–2027.

Whatever your Saturday holds — a costume, a candy bowl, or an early night — stay safe out there, and keep an eye on the roads tonight with the little ones. We'll be back tomorrow morning.

top.title: Bakersfield police searching for suspect in Smoke Bros burglary on Rosedale Highway
